Scope

This is a documentation repository, not an application or library. Its purpose is to guide users through self-hosting software and hardware, with extensive coverage of Docker, Kubernetes, WireGuard, Nextcloud, Raspberry Pi, Grafana, databases, networking, security, IoT, and related ecosystems. The README documents concepts, recommendations, external links, and setup commands.

Public Entry Points

  • README.md — The primary user-facing entry point. It is a large reference and getting-started guide, including documented installation examples for external tools such as Docker, MinIO, WireGuard, Home Assistant, and ESPHome.
  • Getting Started with Self-Hosting.dockerfile — The repository’s only container-build artifact. Its filename indicates a self-hosting setup image or build recipe, but its implementation cannot be determined from the supplied tree.

Core Component

  • Container setup artifact — Getting Started with Self-Hosting.dockerfile
    Provides the repository’s only apparent executable/deployment-oriented surface. The available evidence does not establish its base image, installed packages, entrypoint, ports, volumes, or runtime behavior.

Runtime and State

No application runtime, source modules, service implementation, database schema, or repository-managed persistent state is visible. The README discusses persistent storage, backups, databases, and container volumes as self-hosting concerns, but those are recommendations for externally deployed software rather than evidence of state owned by this repository.

Relationships

The container setup artifact is the only apparent build/deployment surface in the tree. Users consume the guide as reference material and may use its instructions to deploy external systems. Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, cloud providers, operating systems, hardware, and listed projects are external actors or alternatives; they are not shown as bundled repository components or confirmed dependencies.

Extension and Ownership Boundaries

The guide is intentionally extensible through community contributions and issue suggestions, as documented in the project text and supported by CONTRIBUTING.md. New recommendations, tutorials, and platform-specific instructions belong to the documentation-maintenance boundary. Any actual hosting, networking, credentials, application data, and operational responsibility remains with the user’s selected external platforms.
